$comment: The coverage ledger. Every load-bearing claim this system makes about itself names the check that verifies it. audit-system.py reports any claim whose verifier is null or missing from disk. The repo already knew 'skipped is not passed'; this is the generalisation it lacked — UNCHECKED IS NOT PASSED. Every blind spot found on 2026-08-28 was a claim in this shape: asserted, believed, and verified by nothing, while every check that did exist passed.

claims.claim: No value may exist outside tokens.json (the token contract)
claims.how: find_literal_leaks — zero literals above the primitive layer, recursing into composite values

claims.claim: No component may be used that is not in component-index.json (prohibition 1)
claims.how: plants an unindexed component and requires BLOCK; plants an indexed one and requires allow

claims.claim: No user quote may exist outside evidence-ledger.json (prohibition 2)
claims.how: unresolved [E-nnn] in artifacts/ and foundations/ is a blocker
claims.note: PARTIAL — the ledger is empty, so the check has never had a resolvable ID to pass on. Untested in the affirmative.

claims.claim: Gate B blocks off-system writes
claims.how: 12 planted violations across raw hex, raw spacing, components, naming and types

claims.claim: The Stop backstop catches what Gate B cannot see (Bash writes)
claims.how: writes a violation via a shell redirect and requires the backstop to report it

claims.claim: Layer 1 makes off-limits paths impossible
claims.how: The claim as written stays FALSE and cannot be made true: settings.json denies Write/Edit on research/sources/** and cannot deny Bash by path without denying Bash entirely. So prevention is replaced by detection — every raw source is sha256'd into research/sources-manifest.json, and a change, removal or addition fails the check. test-gates.py exercises all three branches: baseline clean must pass, a Bash-altered source must fail, and a Bash-MANUFACTURED source that was never baselined must fail. Wired into CI 2026-09-01.
claims.correction_history: This entry asserted exactly the sentence above on 2026-09-01 while ADDITION was only a warning and the check exited 0. A fabricated source written through a Bash redirect passed CI, and quotes logged against it would have resolved cleanly for ever after — altering testimony was caught, manufacturing it was not, which is the one case that defeats prohibition 2 outright. It was found the same day by an independent system-keeper audit, not by the author, and only because that audit was told to attack the claim rather than read it. test-gates.py case 15 did not cover it: flipping ADDED to blocker in a sandbox left the case still passing, proving it exercised only the MODIFIED branch. Half a guarantee was tested and the whole of it recorded as verified. Kept here rather than overwritten, because the corrected sentence reads identically to the false one and nothing else would show that it was ever wrong.
claims.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01 as detection, not prevention, and the distinction is deliberate. It matters most where the ledger is concerned: if a source can be altered after quotes were logged against it, every citation still resolves — to testimony nobody gave. Tamper-evidence on the sources is what makes 'every quote resolves' mean 'no user was invented'. The check also flags the CITED-vs-uncited distinction, so an altered file the ledger depends on is a blocker rather than a warning.

claims.claim: component-index.json entries satisfy component.schema.json
claims.how: check 4b validates every entry; the adapter refuses to write on violation

claims.claim: Every tokens_used reference resolves to a real token
claims.how: check 4c, paths and globs

claims.claim: No two component entries share a normalised name (ADR-018)
claims.how: collision guard refuses to write; audit-contracts.py reports independently

claims.claim: Regenerating the component index produces an identical file (ADR-013 link 1)
claims.how: CI regenerates design-system/component-index.json with the Carbon adapter and fails on a non-empty git diff, the same idiom already used for .ai/, _registry.json and llms.txt. Confirmed byte-identical locally on 2026-09-01 before wiring.
claims.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01 as a standing test. Previously verified once by hand on 2026-08-28 and never re-run, which is not the same claim — ingest is the bottom of the stack, and if it is not reproducible then nothing built on the index can be trusted to be either. A hand-check that nothing repeats is exactly the 'named layer that reads as coverage' failure.

claims.claim: Light and dark semantic themes carry identical key sets (ADR-001 needs one name per variable mode)
claims.how: symmetry check; the aligner refuses to write unless the sets match exactly

claims.claim: Counts stated in prose match the things they count
claims.how: check 5e against the declared list in validation/declared-counts.json (12 claims across README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, design-system/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md, architecture.md). PARTIAL BY DESIGN: a declared list, not a general prose scanner — a count not named in declared-counts.json is uncovered, and a claim whose sentence is reworded is reported as a stale-pattern warning rather than silently dropped.
claims.note: Re-running the new check on 2026-08-31 found 4 of the 12 declared counts currently wrong: README.md's ADR count (17 vs 19), AGENTS.md's worker count (12 vs 13), and CLAUDE.md's L1-of-total artifact-type count (34 of 40 vs 35 of 41). These are open findings in audit-system.py, not fixed here — see C-010.

claims.claim: Evidence cited by a tracked document is itself tracked
claims.how: the foundations check errors on scratch/ references
claims.note: PARTIAL — covers design-system/foundations/ only. decisions/ is uncovered; see correction C-011.

claims.claim: Artifacts carry resolvable provenance to a token version
claims.how: Check 5f, conditional in both directions: an artifact whose payload references tokens must declare inputs.tokens_version (blocker if absent); one that references none must leave it null (error if set). Negative-tested both ways on 2026-09-01 — stripping ART-008's version blocked, and the check surfaced ART-007, which references typography.scale throughout and had carried null since creation.
claims.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-01, after the claim itself was found to be MIS-SPECIFIED rather than false. It was recorded as 'currently FALSE: every manifest carries tokens_version: null' and the obvious fix was to backfill a version everywhere. That would have manufactured false provenance: five of the thirteen manifests are _templates skeletons, and seven of the eight real artifacts are prose research documents referencing no token at all, so null is the CORRECT value for them. Only ART-007 was genuinely wrong; its version was recovered from the single release tokens.json has ever declared and backfilled with a note, payload untouched. The lesson is the one this ledger keeps teaching: a field that is empty is not automatically a field that is wrong.

claims.claim: The autonomy ladder graduates and demotes task types on evidence
claims.note: UNVERIFIED, and recorded that way after a failed attempt to close it. On 2026-09-01 this was set to verified_by: CLAUDE.md on the grounds that the document now carries a NOT OPERATIVE banner. An independent audit deleted the banner outright and the audit still reported '18 of 18 claims verified' — because naming a file as a verifier only proves the file EXISTS. A claim about a document, verified by that document, is circular; it closed the warning without establishing anything. The banner is still in CLAUDE.md and is still worth having, since prose in the present tense reads as a live mechanism. But it is documentation, not verification, and this field now says so. The ladder remains unimplemented and unverifiable: nothing counts clean reviews, 2 of 40 routing rows have ever been exercised, and its declared tally lives in memory/corrections.md, which is gitignored and would not survive a clone.

claims.claim: Work is routed through the agent roster and its gates
claims.how: ART-008 records produced_by: a11y-checker, dispatched by the orchestrator through the Phase 4 routing row. First artifact of 8 not attributed to main-session. The registry is generated by scanning, so the attribution cannot be hand-written.
claims.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-31, and partially: one artifact of eight came through the roster. The routing table has 40 rows and 2 have now been exercised (system-keeper for validators, a11y-checker for a11y-audit). The claim is no longer false; it is not yet broadly true.

claims.claim: Enforcement layer 3 runs — CI validates the sources of truth, fails on a stale generated file, and runs the whole-repo audit on every push and pull request
claims.how: Observed executing on a real pull request 2026-08-31: 'Gate B / audit (push)' and 'Gate B / audit (pull_request)' both green. The job validates every JSON source of truth, rebuilds .ai/, _registry.json and llms.txt and fails if any was stale, then runs audit-system.py --report.
claims.note: architecture.md records that this layer 'existed only as a sentence until 2026-08-25'. Until this PR it had never been observed running on real work — the workflow file existed and nothing proved it executed. A named layer that has never fired is the coverage illusion this repo was built to remove, so the distinction between 'the file is there' and 'it ran and went green' is the whole point of recording it here.

claims.claim: The token layer can be pushed to Figma variables — ADR-013 link 6, the INVERT link
claims.asserted_in: DESIGN-SYSTEM.md build order step 3 · ADR-001 inversion · ADR-013 link 6
claims.how: CORRECTED 2026-09-02; the previous text said 762 of 794 across 6 collections and every one of those figures had moved. Re-derived today by running the named verifier: validation/figma-representable.py reports 829 tokens total — 797 importable as Figma variables, 12 belonging to a Figma STYLE rather than a variable (8 typography.scale composites, 4 elevation), and 20 with no Figma representation at all (6 motion.duration, 6 motion.easing, 6 motion.transition, 2 density type-scale). The 797 is derived from the token file by script and never asserted. WHAT THIS VERIFIES IS THE REPRESENTABILITY SPLIT ONLY — which tokens CAN cross and which cannot, and that absence is correct rather than a gap. It says nothing about what the Figma file currently holds; that is a separate claim and is carried uncovered as V-024.
claims.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-02 for the representable subset, and the qualification is still the finding: the DTCG-to-Figma-variable mapping is not total, because Figma variables hold only COLOR/FLOAT/STRING/BOOLEAN and every composite type falls outside that. The 32 absences are correct and permanent; a placeholder would not be. LIVE STATE, recorded here as fact and not as verification: file ip2wZ3UUQ5sbFc3r902kYK holds 561 variables across FIVE collections — palette 289, semantic 236, spacing 13, typography 21, density 2 — and `semantic` carries TWO MODES, Light and Dark. The 797 importable rows fold to 561 variables because the 236 semantic-dark rows are the Dark mode of the 236 semantic variables rather than variables of their own. That collapse was done by direct Plugin API calls outside the import path on 2026-09-02 (C-030), which is why the live half of this claim is no longer machine-checkable: validation/check-figma-live.py has read FAIL since and has no concept of modes. DESIGN-SYSTEM.md build order step 3 previously said 'blocked — no Figma file exists', which was three days stale; corrected in the same pass. Read the method note in C-020 before re-verifying anything about the live file: the importer's diff, the exporter and the success summaries were each wrong in one session, so a direct plugin read is the only accepted evidence.

claims.claim: The attestation hash covers every contract file the checks read
claims.note: UNVERIFIED. Recorded here 2026-09-02 rather than left only inside attestation.json's known_open_at_attestation block, where it was invisible to the audit. Check 5g's WIRING list names one file in design-system/contracts/ (figma-representability.json). component.schema.json — which all 216 component-index entries validate against — and figma-code-map.json are outside the hash, so either can be changed without moving it and without prompting an independent pass. This is C-027 sub-defect E-1, deliberately left open by the 2026-09-02 four-fix pass: every change to 5g invalidates the attestation it is part of, and the brief scoped that pass to the printed-hash bypass. Fix is one line — hash design-system/contracts/*.json — and needs its own attested round.

claims.claim: A hook that is registered is a hook that will actually run
claims.asserted_in: CLAUDE.md enforcement layers 2 and 2b · validation/corrections.json C-025
claims.note: UNVERIFIED. Check 2b asks whether .claude/settings.json REGISTERS gate-b.py under PreToolUse and session-check.py under Stop, and it matches on the command STRING. So `gate-b.py.DISABLED`, `true # gate-b.py`, and a matcher switched from Write|Edit to Read all pass, and permissions {"deny": []} counts as a non-empty block. That is the same proves-the-script-not-the-wiring gap one layer down from the one C-025 closed, and test-gates.py passes clean under a neutered matcher because it invokes the hook by absolute path. C-027 sub-defect E-3. Fix: resolve the referenced path and require the file to exist, require the matcher to cover Write and Edit, require a non-empty deny list.

claims.claim: A page published outside this repository that DECLARES a token release cannot fall behind it without the audit saying so
claims.how: Check 5h over validation/published-surfaces.json: an entry whose documents.tokens_version is behind tokens.json's $version warns with both versions and the URL; ahead or uncomparable errors; a malformed entry errors. Verified firing on a real stale page 2026-09-02.
claims.note: NARROWED 2026-09-02 on attestation, having first been written as 'a page cannot fall behind ... without the audit saying so'. That was false and was proved so: switching the one genuinely stale entry to documents: null plus 56 characters of plausible prose turned the warning into '[INFO] 2 of 2 surfaces are current'. The check verifies a DECLARED version against the repository; it cannot verify that the declaration is honest, and it cannot see a published page that was never added to the ledger at all — that case is undetectable from here (F-4). What the row now claims is what 5h does. The gap between them is why this note exists rather than a closure.

claims.claim: A metrics run record cannot claim a live audit unless one actually ran
claims.how: Check 5i, two conditions rather than one. The newest validation/metrics/*.json must carry gates.source == 'live-audit', which collect-metrics.py sets ONLY after the audit subprocess returns; AND the record must not contradict itself — source 'live-audit' alongside verdict 'UNAVAILABLE' or any null count is an ERROR. Both negative-tested 2026-09-02: moving audit-system.py aside yields source 'unavailable', and reinstating the original C-026 bug is caught by the contradiction arm rather than reported as a live run.
claims.note: NARROWED, then the check was WIDENED to meet it. First written as 'gate counts describe the run that produced them' — false, because the failure branch hardcoded source 'live-audit'. Fixing that was not enough: an independent attestation reinstated the bug and showed the record went out self-contradictory (verdict UNAVAILABLE, every count null, source live-audit) while this very check reported 'gate counts derived from a live audit run'. It ruled the narrowing to be moving the goalposts — the row claimed something its named verifier did not verify — and the answer was to make 5i verify it, not to shrink the claim again. What is still NOT claimed: 5i does not re-derive the counts, so a hand-edited record that is internally consistent still passes. Re-deriving them inside the check would make the check its own subject.

claims.claim: The DS fork state in .ai/index.json is derived from the component index, not asserted
claims.asserted_in: CLAUDE.md DS fork · .ai/index.json state · validation/corrections.json C-029
claims.how: The CI step 'Rebuild index and fail if it was stale' re-runs validation/index-system.py and fails on a non-empty git diff of .ai/. ds_fork is now a pure function of component-index.json — RED while zero level-2 entries positively name CoForge as their source — so a committed value that disagrees with the index turns CI red. Negative-tested 2026-09-02: planting one CoForge-authored L2 entry flipped the derived value to REVIEW and dirtied .ai/; component-index.json restored and re-verified by sha256.
claims.note: The generator reports REVIEW, never YELLOW or GREEN. Which fork the project is on is a declared decision under ADR-011 and belongs to a human; a script may report that the stated reason for RED has expired and may not promote the system past it. What this does NOT verify is the membrane itself: authorship is read from the `source` string because component.schema.json records no promotion event, so a hand-written source naming CoForge would be believed. That is the same class of gap as V-019 and is why the default falls towards RED. DISCLOSED 2026-09-02: the authorship test matches a positive 'CoForge' marker in `source`, so a VENDOR row whose source reads 'Ingested by the CoForge Carbon adapter from Carbon React 1.115.0' would be counted as authored here and flip the fork to REVIEW. Left unfixed deliberately — the failure direction is safe (REVIEW asks a human, it never promotes) and changing _l2_authorship() changes what CI accepts, which is Gate A.

claims.claim: The Figma file matches the token layer
claims.asserted_in: design-system/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md build order step 3 · ADR-001 · ADR-013 link 6 · validation/published-surfaces.json (the CoForge Foundations library entry declares tokens_version 0.2.0) · validation/corrections.json C-020, C-030
claims.note: UNVERIFIED — and recorded as uncovered on purpose, because the alternative is silence, and in this repository silence has to mean 'verified' or it means nothing. A check for exactly this exists — validation/check-figma-live.py, built to close C-020 — and it is RED: run 2026-09-02 it returns VERDICT: FAIL, 474 blockers, 323 uncompared. Naming it here would be the V-015 mistake of treating a file's existence as verification, so verified_by stays null until it is repaired. The 474 are not evidence Figma is wrong: 236 report semantic-dark 'MISSING from Figma' when it is in fact the Dark mode of semantic, and 238 are shape artefacts of a capture format the checker does not read. The 323 uncompared are every colour literal, number and string in the file. WHAT IS KNOWN INDEPENDENTLY, and is evidence rather than verification: the 2026-09-02 token-keeper mirror audit re-implemented the bridge from design-system/contracts/figma-representability.json without importing validation/build-figma-tokens.py and compared its own derivation to the capture at (collection, name, mode) — 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 divergent across 797 comparisons, 0 dangling aliases, 0 duplicate (collection, name) pairs. That is a one-off human-run audit of a scratch capture, not a repeatable check in a tracked path, and it does not cover text or effect styles at all (no capture of them exists) or anything in the file that is not a variable. CLOSES when check-figma-live.py is mode-aware, contracts exactly one capture shape, covers the 8 text and 2 effect styles, and reports 0 blockers AND 0 uncompared — Phase 2 of validation/reports/2026-09-02__plan-foundations-figma-migration.md. It will NOT be closed by making the blockers go away: re-importing the current generated file would recreate the deleted collection and turn the check green over a file holding every dark value twice (C-030). STRUCTURAL LIMIT that will remain after Phase 2: layer 3 has no Figma access, so this can never run in CI. It is a local pre-flight, and a claim whose only verifier is local is weaker than one CI enforces.
